matched_details: Party: DEMOCRATIC ALLIANCE in the gazette; reported as the DA's Johannesburg mayoral candidate (IOL 2026-09-06; EWN 2026-09-21).
List position: gazette DA PR rank 1, City of Johannesburg; News24 (2026-11-08) reports the DA PR list as 'topped by Helen Zille'.
Council: City of Johannesburg in both the gazette and the reporting.
identity_match.note: The gazetted name (OTTA HELENE MAREE) differs from the public name (Helen Zille). The link rests on party + PR rank 1 + council, not on the name. No source on the allowed list stating the legal name was found; encyclopaedia and aggregator pages were not used. Reviewers should confirm.

court_matters.value: The Public Protector found that 2017 tweets by Zille about colonialism, made while she was Western Cape premier, violated the Constitution and the Executive Ethics Code. Zille applied for a review of the report; the High Court dismissed it, and she appealed.
court_matters.label: Disputed
court_matters.outcome: The Supreme Court of Appeal upheld Zille's appeal with costs and set aside the High Court's dismissal of her review, on 7 February 2022 (Premier of the Western Cape Province v The Public Protector & Another (771/2020) [2022] ZASCA 16, as cited in The Citizen). Zille said she had apologised for the tweets and was entitled to make them.
